title: Maximum Width Ramp
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> st (monotonic stack of indices): up to n entries → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector nums, returned int
approach: Build a monotonic decreasing stack of candidate left indices: an index `i` is worth keeping only if `nums[i]` is strictly smaller than every earlier candidate, because any later value that is ≥ an earlier candidate is dominated as a left endpoint. Then scan `j` from right to left; while the stack top's value ≤ `nums[j]`, pop it and update the answer with `j - top`. Each index is pushed and popped at most once, so the whole thing is linear.
hints: For two indices i1 < i2 with nums[i1] <= nums[i2], which of them can never be the better left endpoint of a ramp, and why does that mean most indices are not worth keeping as left endpoints?

Use a monotonic decreasing stack of indices (push i only when nums[i] is strictly smaller than the value at the current stack top). For nums = [6,0,8,2,1,5], the stack ends as [0,1] because 8,2,1,5 are all >= 0.

**All equal** - every pair is a valid ramp, so the widest uses the two ends.
`Input: nums = [5,5,5,5]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: pop condition `nums[stack.top] < nums[j]` (strict) → at j=3, 5<5 is false, no pop, returns 0.

**Strictly decreasing (no ramp)** - no i<j satisfies nums[i] <= nums[j].
`Input: nums = [5,4,3,2,1]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: inverted pop trigger `nums[stack.top] >= nums[j]` → at j=4 pops index 0, returns 4.

**Already sorted ascending** - the whole array is one big ramp from end to end.
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,4,5]` → `Expected: 4`
⚠️ Bug: scanning j left-to-right instead of right-to-left → stack=[0] is popped at j=0 with width 0, returns 0.

**Minimum at the end** - the global minimum is the last element, so the best ramp uses an earlier right endpoint.
`Input: nums = [2,3,4,5,1]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: only testing j = n-1 as the right endpoint → nums[4]=1 is smaller than all earlier values, no pop, returns 0.

followUps.q: Return the count of ramps achieving the maximum width, not just the width.
followUps.a: Keep the same monotonic stack and right-to-left scan. While popping, if `j - top` equals the current best, increment a counter; if it exceeds the best, reset the counter to 1. Multiple stack entries can tie for one j, so count each pop separately. TC O(n), SC O(n).

followUps.q: What if nums[i] can be negative?
followUps.a: Nothing changes - the algorithm only compares values with `<=` and `<`, so signs are irrelevant. The monotonic stack and pop condition behave identically. TC O(n), SC O(n).

followUps.q: The array arrives as a stream and you may store only O(√n) elements at a time.
followUps.a: Process in blocks of size √n: keep a monotonic-decreasing list of block minima with their indices, then for each right endpoint scan blocks left-to-right, binary-searching the smallest block whose minimum ≤ nums[j] and scanning within it. TC O(n√n), SC O(√n).
